device.name: Rechargeable sonic electric toothbrush
device.summary: A sealed, induction-charged toothbrush using a resonant magnetic actuator to oscillate a detachable brush head.
device.disclaimer: Representative internals of this kind of device, not an exact copy of one product.

parts.name: Detachable brush neck
parts.function: Transfers shaft motion into the brush head while providing a removable, washable outer neck.
parts.howItWorks: The neck pushes onto the handle nose and locks to the drive coupling. Its hollow tapered wall surrounds the moving shaft without rubbing it. A snap fit lets the complete head assembly be replaced when the bristles wear.
parts.engineering: The neck must remain concentric with the shaft despite molding shrinkage and repeated removal. Running clearance around the shaft is typically a few tenths of a millimetre, while the snap features require controlled elastic strain.

parts.name: Brush head body
parts.function: Supports the bristle plate and protects the head-to-neck joint.
parts.howItWorks: The rounded body is sized to reach back teeth while presenting a smooth surface to the mouth. It moves as one rigid piece with the neck. Its front face carries the bristle plate and its rear blends into the neck.
parts.engineering: Thin walls and generous external radii reduce uncomfortable hard edges. The polymer must tolerate water, toothpaste surfactants and repeated high-frequency acceleration without fatigue cracking.
failureModes: Permanent deformation from excessive brushing force

parts.name: Bristle carrier plate
parts.function: Holds the bristle tufts in a precise pattern on the front of the brush head.
parts.howItWorks: Tufts are anchored into closely spaced holes or molded sockets in the plate. The plate distributes their loads into the head body. In this teardown it is shown separately to expose the tuft anchoring plane.
parts.engineering: Real heads commonly integrate this plate with the body or use an in-mold tufting process. Hole position and tuft retention matter because each filament reverses direction hundreds of times per second.

parts.name: Bristle tuft array
parts.function: Contacts teeth and gums to remove plaque through rapid sweeping motion.
parts.howItWorks: Each visible tuft contains many fine flexible filaments. The actuator sweeps the tufts from side to side while their bending lets them conform to tooth surfaces. Slight differences in trim length help the outer filaments reach around the tooth.
parts.engineering: For small angular shaft motion, tip displacement is approximately x = L·theta, with theta in radians. At L = 90 mm and theta = 0.017 rad, the geometric displacement is about 1.5 mm before bristle flexibility is considered.
failureModes: Worn or poorly rounded filament tips

parts.name: Brush head drive coupling
parts.function: Locks the replaceable head to the oscillating drive shaft.
parts.howItWorks: A socket slides over the flattened shaft tip so torque is transmitted without a separate fastener. Flexible features or an interference fit suppress rattling. Pulling the head axially releases the connection for replacement.
parts.engineering: The coupling combines low insertion force with very small torsional backlash. Repeated fretting at the shaft tip can enlarge the socket, so a wear-resistant polymer and generous fillet radii are useful.

parts.name: Sealed handle housing
parts.function: Forms the water-resistant handle and protects all internal components.
parts.howItWorks: The hollow tapered shell provides the main gripping surface and resists bending loads from brushing. It encloses the actuator, electronics and cell with only small openings for the controls and shaft. Seals at the base and nose keep water outside.
parts.engineering: A representative wall thickness is 1.2–1.5 mm. The long shell needs draft for molding, controlled roundness for the base seal and enough stiffness that hand pressure does not make it rub the moving actuator.

parts.name: Elastomer grip insert
parts.function: Improves wet grip and cushions the hand from vibration.
parts.howItWorks: A soft rear panel sits in a shallow housing recess. Raised ribs increase friction when the handle is wet. The elastomer also provides a small amount of vibration isolation between the shell and the user's hand.
parts.engineering: The insert may be bonded, mechanically keyed or produced by two-shot molding. Its hardness is a compromise between secure grip, cleanability and resistance to tearing at the rib roots.

parts.name: Induction charging base cap
parts.function: Closes the handle base and sits over the external charging stand.
parts.howItWorks: The cap is a solid polymer wall rather than an open electrical socket. An alternating magnetic field passes through it to the receiving coil inside. Its inner spigot aligns the cap and compresses the base seal.
parts.engineering: The cap-to-coil spacing affects both charging efficiency and mechanical protection. Polymer is used instead of metal because a conductive closed shell would support eddy currents and weaken the charging field.

parts.name: Base sealing ring
parts.function: Prevents water from entering through the removable base joint.
parts.howItWorks: The elastomer ring sits in a shallow groove and is squeezed between the cap and housing. Compression creates a continuous sealing line around the base. Unlike a moving seal, it does not experience repeated shaft rubbing.
parts.engineering: Static face or radial seals commonly use roughly 15–25% compression. Groove fill must remain below 100% so the elastomer has somewhere to displace without being cut during assembly.
failureModes: Leakage from toothpaste or grit on the sealing face

parts.name: Power and mode button
parts.function: Provides the user's sealed mechanical input for starting, stopping and selecting modes.
parts.howItWorks: Pressing the outer button moves a short stem against the flexible membrane beneath it. The membrane transmits the force to a small switch on the circuit board. Releasing the button lets the elastomer return it to its rest position.
parts.engineering: Button travel is kept small to limit the housing opening and membrane strain. The assembly must provide tactile feedback without creating a direct leak path around the stem.

parts.name: Indicator light pipe
parts.function: Carries light from an internal LED to the handle surface.
parts.howItWorks: The clear polymer rod captures light from the LED below it. Internal reflections guide much of that light to the visible outer face. It communicates operating or charging status without placing an electrical component at the housing surface.
parts.engineering: A small air gap and polished optical faces improve transmission, while the surrounding geometry limits stray light. The pipe also needs mechanical support so it cannot press on and damage the LED.
failureModes: Stress cracking around the housing opening

parts.name: Waterproof button membrane
parts.function: Seals the control opening while transmitting button motion to the board switch.
parts.howItWorks: A thin silicone flange is trapped against the housing and a flexible dome sits over the switch. The dome deflects when pressed, then supplies the return force. The continuous sheet keeps water away from the switch contacts.
parts.engineering: Dome thickness controls actuation force and fatigue life. Compression around the flange must be continuous; a screw boss or molding witness line crossing the sealing land can create a leak.

parts.name: Internal structural chassis
parts.function: Locates the cell, circuit board, actuator and shaft supports as one rigid assembly.
parts.howItWorks: A rear spine and several annular cradles hold components at fixed positions inside the round handle. The chassis carries brushing loads from the shaft bearings into the housing. It also keeps heavy parts from moving and fatiguing their wires.
parts.engineering: Bearing alignment is more important than the chassis's absolute appearance. The design balances stiffness, moldability and open space for wiring; thin ribs are preferred to thick sections that could sink or warp during molding.
failureModes: Loose component mounts and vibration noise

parts.name: Chassis retaining screws
parts.function: Clamp the upper carrier and maintain alignment of the internal assembly.
parts.howItWorks: Two small screws draw the upper support against the chassis. Their clamp load prevents the bearing carrier from shifting under vibration. They are removed before the shaft and actuator supports can be separated.
parts.engineering: Screws into polymer require controlled boss diameter, engagement length and installation torque. Excess torque can strip the thread or crack a boss; too little allows fretting and noise.

parts.name: Nose and seal carrier
parts.function: Centres the dynamic shaft seal and closes the top of the internal chassis.
parts.howItWorks: The carrier registers inside the housing nose and provides a rigid bore around the seal. Its outer ring reacts brushing loads into the chassis. The central opening leaves room for the shaft to oscillate.
parts.engineering: The carrier controls seal concentricity and compression independently of the flexible outer housing. A stepped bore also prevents the seal from being pushed out by water pressure or shaft motion.

parts.name: Dynamic shaft seal
parts.function: Blocks water and toothpaste while allowing the drive shaft to oscillate.
parts.howItWorks: A flexible lip lightly contacts the moving shaft and follows its small angular and lateral motion. The outer diameter is fixed in the seal carrier. This is the main barrier between the wet brush head and the dry actuator compartment.
parts.engineering: Seal friction consumes actuator power and generates heat, so lip interference is very small. Shaft surface finish, lubricant compatibility and concentricity strongly affect both leakage and wear.
failureModes: Hardening or swelling from chemical exposure

parts.name: Upper shaft bushing
parts.function: Supports the shaft close to the wet end and reacts brushing side loads.
parts.howItWorks: A low-friction sleeve surrounds the shaft while leaving it free to oscillate. Its position near the head reduces shaft bending and keeps the dynamic seal aligned. The outer sleeve is fixed in the upper chassis cradle.
parts.engineering: A representative running diametral clearance is 0.03–0.10 mm, depending on material and manufacturing process. The two shaft supports must be coaxial; misalignment raises friction and can rapidly wear the seal.
parts.material: Stainless carrier with low-friction polymer liner

parts.name: Lower shaft bushing
parts.function: Provides the second shaft support and establishes the actuator's rotation axis.
parts.howItWorks: The lower sleeve works with the upper bushing to resist tilting of the shaft. It sits below the magnetic rotor and close to the torsion spring. The shaft rotates through a small angle rather than continuously spinning.
parts.engineering: Spacing the two supports apart reduces angular error caused by bearing clearance. Low friction is important because the actuator operates near resonance and bearing losses directly reduce amplitude.
parts.material: Sintered bronze or low-friction engineering polymer

parts.name: Oscillating drive shaft
parts.function: Carries alternating torque from the magnetic rotor to the removable brush head.
parts.howItWorks: The slim shaft is supported at two points and twists or rocks through a small angle. Its flattened upper tip engages the head coupling. Its lower region is rigidly attached to the actuator rotor and spring.
parts.engineering: The shaft needs adequate torsional stiffness without adding excessive rotary inertia. For a circular shaft, torsional stiffness is k = G·J/L and J = pi·d^4/32; however, the usable output angle is limited by bearings, seal friction and head load.

parts.name: Laminated actuator stator
parts.function: Guides magnetic flux from the field coils toward the moving magnets.
parts.howItWorks: The soft-magnetic core provides a low-reluctance path around the two coils and ends in pole faces near the rotor magnets. Reversing coil current changes the magnetic polarity at those faces. The stationary core also conducts some coil heat into the chassis.
parts.engineering: The exact pole geometry varies considerably between toothbrush designs. Lamination or another loss-control strategy reduces eddy-current heating; tight pole gaps increase force but leave less tolerance for rotor runout.

parts.name: Actuator field coils
parts.function: Convert controlled alternating current into the magnetic field that drives the rotor.
parts.howItWorks: Two copper windings sit on opposite stator limbs. The electronic driver reverses or redistributes their current at the actuator's operating frequency. Their changing field pulls and pushes the permanent-magnet rotor in alternating directions.
parts.engineering: Each winding obeys v = R·i + L·di/dt, with an additional motion-induced voltage. Copper loss is Pcu = I_rms^2·R. The model shows a small number of visible turns; a real winding contains many more turns of finer wire.

parts.name: Magnet carrier rotor
parts.function: Holds the drive magnets and couples their alternating force into the shaft.
parts.howItWorks: The carrier is fixed to the shaft and places a magnet on each side of its axis. Magnetic forces at this offset create a torque about the shaft. The carrier reverses direction on every half-cycle instead of rotating continuously.
parts.engineering: Rotor inertia helps set the resonant frequency, so unnecessary mass is undesirable. Magnet retention must survive repeated acceleration without allowing a magnet to shift into a stator pole.

parts.name: Actuator permanent magnets
parts.function: Provide the fixed magnetic poles on which the stator field acts.
parts.howItWorks: The two magnets present opposite pole orientations to the nearby stator faces. As coil current changes, attraction and repulsion produce an alternating torque. Their rigid attachment ensures that this torque reaches the rotor and shaft.
parts.engineering: High remanence gives useful force in a small volume, but the adhesive joint and corrosion protection are critical. Excess temperature, mechanical impact or exposure to water can permanently reduce magnetic performance.

parts.name: Resonant torsion spring
parts.function: Returns the rotor toward centre and stores energy between oscillation half-cycles.
parts.howItWorks: One side of the spring reacts against the chassis and the other against the moving shaft assembly. Deflection stores elastic energy and creates a restoring torque. Together with rotor inertia, it sets the frequency at which the toothbrush moves most efficiently.
parts.engineering: For torsional stiffness kt and total reflected inertia J, the undamped natural frequency is f0 = sqrt(kt/J)/(2·pi). Operating near f0 increases amplitude for a given input, but worn bearings, head load and temperature shift the response.

parts.name: Brushing pressure sensor
parts.function: Detects excessive brushing force so the controller can warn the user or reduce motion.
parts.howItWorks: A representative strain-sensing element sits beside the upper shaft support. Side load on the brush head slightly deflects this support and changes the sensor signal. The controller filters that signal and compares it with a pressure threshold.
parts.engineering: Some toothbrushes instead infer pressure from actuator current, so this separate sensor is only one representative implementation. Signal drift, mounting stiffness and head mass must be accounted for during calibration.
parts.material: Silicon sensing element on a metal and polymer carrier

parts.name: Main control and charging board
parts.function: Hosts the charging, battery-management, control and actuator-drive electronics.
parts.howItWorks: The narrow vertical board connects the receiving coil, cell, user switch and actuator. Charging circuitry rectifies the coil output and regulates cell charging. During brushing, logic and power electronics generate the required coil current while timing the brushing session.
parts.engineering: The board is long and narrow to fit beside the cell and within the curved housing. Power components require copper area for heat spreading, while wet-service reliability depends on cleaning flux residues and preventing moisture-driven electrochemical migration.
parts.material: FR-4 circuit board with copper traces

specs.label: Functions
specs.value: charging, protection, control and power drive

parts.name: Controller integrated circuit
parts.function: Runs the brushing timer, reads inputs and coordinates drive and indicator behaviour.
parts.howItWorks: The controller detects button presses and optionally reads the pressure sensor. It produces timed gate signals for the power driver and changes patterns for different modes. It also manages reminders, automatic shutoff and low-battery indication.
parts.engineering: A small low-power controller is sufficient; its clock need not directly determine resonance if the drive uses feedback. Firmware commonly includes debounce, cell-voltage checks and fault handling to prevent continuous unintended coil current.
parts.material: Silicon integrated circuit in a molded package

specs.label: Typical functions
specs.value: timing, input handling, modulation and status

parts.name: Actuator power driver
parts.function: Switches cell power through the actuator coils in the required direction and timing.
parts.howItWorks: Power switches inside the driver connect the winding to the supply in alternating polarities. The controller's low-power signals determine when the switches operate. Current limiting and flyback handling protect both the switches and the battery.
parts.engineering: An H-bridge applies +V or -V to a load, enabling bidirectional current without a dual supply. Switch loss is approximately Pcond = I_rms^2·RDS(on) per conducting device, plus switching loss during each transition.

parts.name: Status indicator LED
parts.function: Produces the light used to indicate operation, charging or low battery.
parts.howItWorks: The controller switches a small current through the light-emitting diode. The light pipe above it carries that light through the sealed housing. Different flashing patterns can communicate status with only one optical window.
parts.engineering: A series resistor or controlled current source sets LED current. Brightness is limited by both user comfort and battery energy, especially during long charging indications.
failureModes: Optical misalignment with the light pipe

parts.name: Rechargeable lithium-ion cell
parts.function: Stores electrical energy for cordless brushing sessions.
parts.howItWorks: The cylindrical cell is charged through the induction receiver and charging electronics. During use it supplies the actuator driver and control circuitry. Protection and charge control keep its voltage and current within safe limits.
parts.engineering: Usable runtime is approximately t = eta·Vnom·C/Pavg, with capacity C in Ah. Mechanical retention must prevent the relatively heavy cell from hammering its contacts during drops, and the charging system must not continue charging a damaged or excessively hot cell.
parts.material: Lithium-ion cell with steel can and polymer sleeve

parts.name: Cell contact springs
parts.function: Maintain low-resistance electrical connections to both ends of the removable cell.
parts.howItWorks: Springy metal strips press against the cell terminals and connect them to the board wiring. Their compliance tolerates dimensional variation and small impacts. The contact force must remain high enough to prevent intermittent power during vibration.
parts.engineering: Contact resistance causes local heating according to P = I^2·Rcontact. Nickel plating improves corrosion resistance, while adequate elastic deflection prevents relaxation and fretting over the product life.

parts.name: Internal flexible wiring
parts.function: Connects components that cannot be mounted directly on the rigid circuit board.
parts.howItWorks: Insulated conductors join the cell contacts, charging receiver, actuator coils and optional sensor to the board. Gentle bends provide strain relief and leave space for assembly. Routing keeps wires clear of the moving rotor and shaft.
parts.engineering: Wire length is a compromise between serviceability and resistance. High-vibration joints need strain relief; repeated bending concentrated directly at a solder joint is a common source of open circuits.
failureModes: Broken conductor at a solder joint
Wire trapped in the moving actuator

parts.name: Induction receiving coil
parts.function: Receives energy wirelessly from the charging stand through the sealed base.
parts.howItWorks: An alternating magnetic field from the stand crosses the flat spiral winding and induces an alternating voltage. The board rectifies and regulates that voltage to charge the cell. No exposed metal charging contacts are required.
parts.engineering: For sinusoidal excitation, the open-circuit receiver voltage magnitude is approximately |V2| = omega·M·|I1|, where M is mutual inductance. Coil alignment, base thickness and ferrite properties strongly affect M and charging efficiency.
failureModes: Heat damage from a shorted turn

parts.name: Receiver ferrite backing
parts.function: Concentrates the charging magnetic field and shields nearby components from it.
parts.howItWorks: The high-permeability disc sits just behind the receiving coil. It provides an easier return path for magnetic flux and increases coupling to the charging stand. It also reduces unwanted alternating field penetration into the cell and chassis region.
parts.engineering: Ferrite offers high magnetic permeability with much lower electrical conductivity than steel, limiting eddy-current loss. It is brittle, so the chassis must support it without creating concentrated bending stress.
failureModes: Reduced charging efficiency from incorrect placement

systems.name: Wireless charging path
systems.explanation: The receiving coil produces AC in the charger's magnetic field; the board rectifies and regulates it before delivering controlled charge current to the cell.

systems.name: Actuator power path
systems.explanation: Stored cell energy passes through protection and switching electronics, then the bidirectional driver energizes the field coils with timed alternating current.

systems.name: User command and drive control
systems.explanation: A button press becomes a logic input; the controller selects a mode and timing pattern, and the power driver turns those low-power commands into coil excitation.

systems.name: Magnetic torque to bristle motion
systems.explanation: The coil-stator field exerts force on the rotor magnets, producing alternating shaft torque that passes through the replaceable-head coupling and sweeps the bristles.

systems.name: Actuator heat path
systems.explanation: Copper and magnetic losses warm the actuator; conduction through its mounting and chassis spreads that heat before it dissipates through the handle surface.

steps.title: Remove the replaceable brush head
steps.narration: Pull the head straight off the shaft. The exploded head separates into its neck, body, bristle carrier, tufts and drive coupling so the motion interface is visible.

steps.title: Open the sealed charging base
steps.narration: Release the base cap and its static sealing ring. Beneath them are the flat receiving coil and ferrite backing, with no exposed electrical charging contacts.

steps.title: Slide away the handle enclosure
steps.narration: Remove the outer housing, soft grip and surface controls. The waterproof membrane and light pipe show how user interaction crosses the enclosure without leaving an open electrical path.

steps.title: Release the upper internal carrier
steps.narration: Take out the retaining screws, button membrane and nose carrier. The internal chassis now exposes the aligned shaft supports and the compact actuator below them.

steps.title: Extract the shaft and dynamic seal
steps.narration: Lift out the shaft, its two bushings and the flexible water seal. Notice that the wet brush interface is separated from the electrical compartment by a very small moving contact zone.

steps.title: Disassemble the resonant actuator
steps.narration: Separate the field coils, magnetic core, magnets, rotor carrier and torsion spring. These parts exchange electrical and elastic energy to create efficient high-frequency oscillation.

steps.title: Free the electronics and energy storage
steps.narration: Disconnect the flexible wiring and remove the cell, contacts and populated board. The charging receiver, power driver and controller all serve the single cell and actuator.

steps.title: Review the structural backbone
steps.narration: The bare chassis remains as the alignment reference for the entire product. Its bearing locations, component cradles and load path are as important as the electronic parts it carried.

study.overview: This toothbrush stores energy in a small rechargeable lithium-ion cell. Placing the sealed handle on its stand couples magnetic energy into a coil at the base, and the control board uses that energy to charge the cell. When the button is pressed, a controller and bidirectional power driver energize two actuator coils. Their changing magnetic field applies alternating torque to permanent magnets on the shaft. A torsion spring and the moving mass form a resonant system, so modest electrical input can produce rapid bristle motion. Two bushings keep the shaft aligned, while a flexible lip seal transmits that motion through a water barrier. The replaceable head couples to the shaft tip, and the bristles sweep across the teeth. A pressure sensor or actuator-current estimate can detect excessive force, and the indicator reports operating and charging status.

keyConcepts.title: Oscillation rather than continuous rotation
keyConcepts.body: A sonic toothbrush does not need its head to spin through full revolutions. The actuator repeatedly reverses a small shaft angle, and the long distance from shaft to bristles converts that angle into useful linear sweep.

keyConcepts.title: Resonance saves actuator power
keyConcepts.body: The torsion spring stores energy as the rotor moves away from centre and returns it on the next half-cycle. Near the natural frequency, the electronics mainly replace energy lost to bristle drag, bearings and seal friction.

keyConcepts.title: A moving seal is a critical compromise
keyConcepts.body: The shaft seal must be tight enough to block contaminated water but gentle enough not to waste torque. Its friction, alignment and wear directly affect battery life, motion amplitude and long-term leakage.

keyConcepts.title: Inductive charging enables a sealed base
keyConcepts.body: Energy crosses the polymer base as an alternating magnetic field. Eliminating exposed contacts improves water resistance, but charging speed depends on coil alignment, spacing and power conversion losses.

keyConcepts.title: The driver controls current, not just voltage
keyConcepts.body: The coils are inductive, so current does not change instantly. The power stage applies alternating voltage while handling stored magnetic energy and limiting current to protect the windings, switches and cell.

keyConcepts.title: Pressure feedback protects teeth and hardware
keyConcepts.body: Excessive force increases bristle drag, shaft side load and actuator current. A sensor or current-based estimate lets the controller warn the user or reduce drive before the brushing experience and mechanism suffer.

keyConcepts.title: Alignment is a system-level requirement
keyConcepts.body: The chassis, two shaft supports, seal and head coupling form one precision chain. A small displacement that seems harmless in a molded support can cause seal wear, pole-face rubbing, noise or reduced amplitude.

principles.title: Torsional resonance
principles.body: The simplified actuator is an inertia-spring system: f0 = (1/(2·pi))·sqrt(kt/J), where kt is torsional stiffness in N·m/rad and J is total rotary inertia in kg·m^2. Increasing J lowers f0; increasing kt raises it. Damping and head loading reduce the peak amplitude and shift the practical best drive point.

principles.title: Bristle displacement from shaft angle
principles.body: For small angles, a point at radius L from the shaft moves approximately x = L·theta, with theta in radians. A shaft amplitude of 1 degree is 0.01745 rad, so at L = 90 mm the ideal tip amplitude is about 1.57 mm. Flexible bristles and contact with teeth modify this free-air value.

principles.title: Coil voltage and copper loss
principles.body: A winding approximately follows v = R·i + L·di/dt + e_motion. The inductance term limits how quickly current can reverse, while e_motion represents the voltage induced by rotor movement. Heat from winding resistance is Pcu = I_rms^2·R, so excessive current reduces both runtime and insulation life.

principles.title: Inductive power transfer
principles.body: For a sinusoidal transmitter current, receiver open-circuit voltage magnitude is approximately |V2| = omega·M·|I1|. Mutual inductance M depends on turns, geometry, separation and alignment. After rectification and regulation, only part of the transmitted power reaches the cell; the remainder becomes heat in the coils and electronics.

principles.title: Battery runtime estimate
principles.body: Cell energy is approximately E = Vnom·C when C is expressed in Ah, giving watt-hours. Average runtime is t = eta·E/Pavg. For example, a 3.6 V, 0.8 Ah cell stores about 2.88 Wh before conversion losses; actuator amplitude, brushing pressure and battery age all change the usable result.

glossary.definition: A device that converts electrical or another form of input energy into controlled mechanical motion.
Lost motion or play at a coupling, noticeable when the direction of torque reverses.
A sleeve bearing that supports a shaft through sliding contact rather than rolling elements.
A seal that maintains a fluid barrier while one of its contacting surfaces moves.
A high-permeability, electrically resistive ceramic magnetic material used to guide alternating magnetic flux.
An arrangement of power switches that can apply either voltage polarity across a load.
Contactless energy transfer between coils using a changing magnetic field.
A transparent optical component that guides light from a source to a remote visible surface.
A measure of how strongly changing current in one coil induces voltage in another.
Enhanced oscillatory response near the natural frequency set by a system's stiffness, inertia and damping.
The moving magnetic or mechanical assembly; here it oscillates rather than rotating continuously.
The stationary magnetic structure that guides flux and supports the field windings.
A spring that supplies restoring torque in proportion to angular deflection.
Geometry or support that prevents cable bending and pulling loads from concentrating at an electrical termination.

quiz.question: Why can a resonant spring-mass actuator produce useful bristle motion with relatively little average electrical power?
options: It eliminates all bearing and seal friction
It exchanges stored energy between spring and inertia, so the supply mainly replaces losses
It lets the cell deliver a higher nominal voltage
It removes the need for a magnetic field
quiz.explanation: Near resonance, energy alternates between rotor motion and spring deflection. The electronics still supply losses from drag, friction and magnetic or resistive heating.

quiz.question: What is the main advantage of induction charging in this product?
options: It guarantees unlimited charging current
It makes the battery unnecessary
It allows charging through a sealed polymer base without exposed contacts
It makes the brush head oscillate
quiz.explanation: Magnetic coupling crosses the base wall, avoiding a wet exposed connector. It does not eliminate conversion losses or the need for a cell.

quiz.question: If rotor inertia increases while torsional stiffness stays constant, what happens to the ideal natural frequency?
options: It decreases
It increases
It stays exactly constant
It becomes zero for any inertia increase
quiz.explanation: Since f0 = sqrt(kt/J)/(2·pi), increasing J reduces the natural frequency.

quiz.question: Why is the shaft seal allowed only a small amount of lip interference?
options: To make the shaft electrically conductive
To increase the cell capacity
To balance water exclusion against friction, wear and lost actuator power
To let toothpaste enter and lubricate the motor
quiz.explanation: More interference can improve sealing initially but increases drag and wear. The design needs enough contact for sealing without excessive loss.

quiz.question: What is the power driver's essential role?
options: To apply controlled bidirectional excitation to the inductive actuator load
To anchor the bristle filaments
To align the two charging coils mechanically
To provide the main water seal
quiz.explanation: The power switches convert controller commands into higher-power coil excitation and handle the winding's inductive behaviour.

quiz.question: Why do the upper and lower shaft supports need good coaxial alignment?
options: Misalignment can raise friction, cause rattling and accelerate seal wear
Alignment only affects the handle colour
It is needed to reverse battery polarity
It determines whether the bristles are nylon
quiz.explanation: The two bushings define the shaft axis. Angular or positional error can bind the shaft and move the seal contact unevenly.

quiz.question: A toothbrush develops much lower amplitude and higher coil temperature under load. Which explanation is most physically consistent?
options: The load has reduced all electrical resistance to zero
Increased damping and friction require more input power while reducing useful motion
The bristle length no longer affects displacement
The ferrite disc has started generating bristle torque directly
quiz.explanation: Extra drag and possible rubbing dissipate more actuator input as heat, leaving less energy in useful oscillation and moving the system away from efficient operation.
